2. This criminal revision under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C., has been filed aggrieved by judgment and order dated 29.07.1994.

The IXth Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Moradabad vide order dated 07.02.1994 passed in Case No. 748 of 1993 convicted respondent under Section 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 7 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1954") and sentenced him to undergo six months rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs. 1000/- and in case of default of payment of fine, he shall further suffer two months rigorous imprisonment.

entities.text: IXth Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Moradabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Thereagainst,
accused preferred Criminal Appeal No. 15 of 1994 which was dismissed vide impugned judgment dated 29.07.1994 and confirmed the judgement and order dated 07.02.1994 passed by Court below.
Being aggrieved, accused-appellant preferred present revision.

Umrao vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146152635/
1 3.

It is contended that there was no compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 and only on the basis that a copy of report was sent to accused and adduced by department as evidence without proving that notice was actually sent to revisionist.
Court below has treated to be a compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 which is wholly illegal, inasmuch as, the law is now well settled for compliance of said section.
Mere sending of notice is not sufficient but prosecution has to prove its service/receipt upon accused.

4. On the question of compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954, I find that Lower Appellate Court has discussed this issue in para-14 which reads as under:-
"14.
The learned counsel for the appellant argued that in the present case the provisions of Section 13(2) have also not been complied with.

In this respect I would like to mention that the Food Clerk P.W. 3 Pramod Kumar has proved it beyond all reasonable doubts that in compliance of Section 13(2) of P.F.A. Act notice alongwith the copy of the report of Public Analyst was sent to the accused.

There is nothing in the evidence of this witness to distrust him and therefore, I am of the view that it is a case in which the provisions of Section 13(2) of P.F.A. Act were fully complied with and there is nothing on the record which makes the accused entitled for acquittal on this account."

5. From a perusal of above paragraph, it is evident that Court below has treated sufficient compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 when notice along with a copy of Analyst report was sent to accused.

However, in my view, service of notice upon accused was necessary to be proved by Prosecution so as to prove compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 and in absence of such evidence,
proceedings are vitiated in law.

I am fortified in taking above view from recent Supreme Court's Judgement in Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019) (Arising out of S.L.P. (Criminal) No. 4314 of 2015) decided on 31.07.2019. In para 15 of judgment

entities.text: Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, Court has said as under:
"The very purpose of furnishing such report is to enable the Accused to seek for reference to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis if the Accused is dissatisfied with the report.
Such safeguard provided to the Accused Under Section 13(2) of the Act is a valuable right.

In that view even if the despatch of the report on 07.04.1980 is taken as substantial compliance though it is beyond the period of 10 days from 18.03.1980 i.e., the date on which the prosecution was lodged, in the absence of there being proof of delivery of the report to the Accused; in the instant facts the valuable right available to the Accused/Appellant to seek for reference within the period of 10 days stands defeated.
In that circumstance when the Appellant/Accused is made to suffer the penal consequences, it will have to be construed strictly.

In the facts and circumstances of this case, since as already noticed above the report of the Analyst has not in fact been served on the Appellant and the mere despatch of the report as per the statement of PW-2 was not sufficient."
(emphasis added)

2 6.
In view thereof, application is allowed.
Impugned judgements of Courts below are hereby set aside.
7. Certify the judgment to the Court below immediately.
